capabilities: Convert PDFs to Markdown via right-click in the file browser
Convert images embedded in notes and insert recognized text below them
Render recognized equations as Obsidian LaTeX ($...$ and $$...$$)
Switch between cloud AI providers and a free local Ollama model
Configure DPI, timeout, retries, and output file conflict handling
extras: API keys are read from environment variables only and never stored on disk; a completely free local path via Ollama (glm-ocr:bf16, ~6s/page, runs on an RTX 2060) is documented alongside paid providers, with per-model cost and quality benchmarks.
motivation: The author loved handwriting notes on an iFlytek Smart Notebook but found organizing them in Obsidian frustrating because the native OCR failed at math formulas.
problem: Obsidian's native OCR handles handwritten mathematical formulas poorly, making it hard to turn handwritten notes into clean Markdown.

requires.name: Ollama (for the free local glm-ocr option)

summary: Converts handwritten PDFs and images to Markdown with LaTeX formulas using vision language models from OpenAI, Qwen, Claude, Gemini, or local Ollama.
